run.topic: What If a Human Grew to the Size of an Elephant??

opening_actions: The scholar places a small human model and an elephant-sized human model beside matching warm plates.
He compares the visible warmth loss from the two body shapes.
He pauses and notices the larger model changing differently.

entry_bridge.a_end: The scholar places the large model beside the small one.
entry_bridge.b_start: A closed topic-styled book rests beside the models.
entry_bridge.reveal: The book reveals a body-size comparison world where scale changes how bodies handle heat.
entry_bridge.world_entry: Two giant and small body outlines stand beside temperature markers in the illustrated topic world.

script_plan.opening_question_spark: If a human grew huge, would their body cool the same?
script_plan.book_transition: Bigger size can change how a body loses heat.
body: Two body outlines show different heat loss.
Small and giant models lose warmth at different speeds.
The giant model has more outside area and loses heat.
The inner part of the body grows differently from outside area.
The square-cube rule explains size changes outside area and volume.
Volume means the space inside a body.
An elephant-sized human may struggle with body heat.
The models show bigger bodies change beyond height.
A giant human is not just a larger copy.
script_plan.full_narration: If a human grew huge, would their body cool the same? Bigger size can change how a body loses heat. Two body outlines show different heat loss. Small and giant models lose warmth at different speeds. The giant model has more outside area and loses heat. The inner part of the body grows differently from outside area. The square-cube rule explains size changes outside area and volume. Volume means the space inside a body. An elephant-sized human may struggle with body heat. The models show bigger bodies change beyond height. A giant human is not just a larger copy. Bodies need new solutions. Suggest next topic in comments.
